items.source: A2-4B Kelime Listesi (Turkishle coursebook + vocab page)
items.notes: Spelling checked against the A2 master coursebook and then TDK: the list has "İlahi" unaccented, glossed "chant". Circumflexes would be wrong here, and not merely unnecessary. TDK lists every sense as one Arabic word (ilāhī) and spells both the adjective and the noun plain "ilahi"; only the vocative "Ey Allah'ım" takes İlahî. The senses differ in sound, not spelling: the adjective "divine" is ila:hi: with a LONG final i, this noun is ila:hi with a SHORT one, and the interjection is i'la:hi, stressed on the first syllable. So an î on this card would assert length the hymn does not have. In all senses the l is palatalised ("l ince okunur"). Corrects an earlier note of mine that called ilâhî a different word — it is the same word, and that is not TDK's spelling of it. TDK lists three homographs with three pronunciations: the adjective 'divine' is ila:hi: (both vowels long), the exclamation is i'la:hi (initial stress), and this noun — the hymn — is ila:hi, so the long a is followed by a SHORT final i. The 'l ince okunur' note makes the l clear despite the back vowel. en.wiktionary's /iˈlaː.hiː/ transcribes the adjective, not this entry.

items.source: A2-4B coursebook vocabulary list, carded as “türkü / halk müziği” in a list of music genres
items.notes: Split from türkü (issue #48). The row pairs them, but they are not synonyms: halk müziği is the genre, listed beside klasik müzik and rock müzik; türkü is a single folk song. A slash entry would also have demanded both forms for one prompt.

A2-4C coursebook dialogue (Kaan Tan interview, “içimdeki duyguları”); not in any unit vocabulary list
items.notes: Spotted missing from a Turkishle "are you B1?" video, where it was the only unknown word. Turkishle never teaches it at any level: the base appears only inflected inside texts — the A2-4C interview, the A2-5C reading, the Ünite 5 exam — and as the personal name Duygu in the A2 -mIş examples, while B1.1 teaches duygusal in a text and duygulandırmak in a vocabulary list. Same pattern as yağmur against yağmurlu: the derivative gets a row, the base never does. Filed under A2-4C, its first occurrence, with no -extra marker, matching ilk, göre and ofis — the marker is reserved for gap-fills that are not in the book at all, and this one is.
